title: An anatomy-informed CT phenotype estimates extrapancreatic perineural-invasion risk in pancreatic cancer
summary: The locked PROPHET model used tumor-vessel spatial features from CT to estimate pathologically confirmed extrapancreatic perineural invasion (EPNI) in resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Across 1,854 patients, reported AUCs included 0.92 in prospective external testing and 0.85 in retrospective external testing; in a reader study, score-plus-visualization assistance increased mean sensitivity from 82% to 93% and reduced reading time. This is an association and diagnostic-support result, not evidence of treatment benefit or direct visualization of nerves. It concerns a related but distinct imaging study from the active catalog record on MRI prediction of perineural invasion (2026-10-machine-learning-models-integrating-2d-and-3d-intratumo--frai-2026-1975752); overlap in clinical endpoint is possible, while modality and reported model result differ.
ai_technology: PROPHET is a locked interpretable machine-learning model deriving an anatomy-informed CT spatial phenotype associated with pathologically confirmed EPNI.
organization: Changhai Hospital; Shanghai General Hospital; Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center; other participating institutions listed by the source

evidence.tested: Multicenter testing included prospective and retrospective external cohorts, neoadjuvant and internal cohorts, and TCIA; six radiologists were assessed with and without combined score-and-visualization assistance.
evidence.unknown: The population comprised resected cases; the observational survival association does not establish causality or treatment benefit. TCIA specificity was low (2/19). Reader improvement cannot be attributed to the score or visualization separately. Similar perineural-invasion endpoint to active MRI record noted; distinct source and CT-based result.
evidence.ai_role: PROPHET is a locked interpretable machine-learning model deriving an anatomy-informed CT spatial phenotype associated with pathologically confirmed EPNI.
